items.title: US sailors arrive in Thailand's Pattaya after record 250 days at sea
items.description: The USS Abraham Lincoln is docking close to Pattaya, known for its neon-lit nightlife, and for sex tourism.

items.title: Why US troops have a history in this raucous Thai city
items.description: The BBC's Jonathan Head looks at the historical echoes of US troops arriving in Pattaya, a beach resort famous for its racy bars.

items.title: Thousands still missing as Nepal-Tibet flood relief and recovery intensifies
items.description: More than 1, 000 people have died and thousands are missing, with communities relying on airlifted supplies.

items.title: BBC travels inside occupied Lebanon as officials say Israel expanding positions
items.description: A BBC team joined a humanitarian mission of the UN peacekeeping force, which says Israeli troops are fortifying positions and continuing demolitions.

items.title: Zelensky says airlines should avoid Russian airspace as Ukraine escalates drone operations
items.description: Chinese and Gulf state airlines are among those still using Russian airspace. Meanwhile, Russia says it will intensify its own attacks on Ukraine.

items.title: Bus crash on Egypt's Red Sea coast kills 22
items.description: Reports say Jordanian nationals are among those killed in the accident in the South Sinai governorate.

items.title: Charlie Kirk murder suspect pleads not guilty as judge clears way for death penalty trial
items.description: The 23-year-old is charged with aggravated murder, a capital offence in Utah, and six other counts.

items.title: South Korea jails care home head for sexually assaulting disabled residents
items.description: The man, surnamed Kim, was handed a 15-year prison term for abusing three residents at the facility near Seoul.

items.title: Tiger Woods to change plea after crash arrest
items.description: The golfer will be in court on Wednesday for a hearing to change his plea after being charged with driving under the influence.

items.title: Guinea-Bissau referendum approves new constitution that expands president's powers
items.description: The sweeping reforms come in the wake of last year's coup and ahead of a proposed return to civilian rule.

items.title: River water smashed into tunnel and chased me for 20 minutes, Nepal worker tells BBC
items.description: Major efforts to rescue hydropower workers continue as Nepal's death toll exceeds 1,000.

items.title: Jailed HK activist Joshua Wong pleads guilty to foreign collusion
items.description: Wong, 29, is already in prison on subversion charges under the controversial National Security Law.

items.title: Germany says Russia behind Leipzig airport drone attack
items.description: A drone carrying an explosive device was discovered at the airport close to Ukrainian cargo planes on 4 August.

items.title: Apple Maps renames Lake Ontario as Lake America after Trump order
items.description: The iPhone maker follows rival technology giant Google in relabelling the Great Lake.

items.title: Ariana Grande makes emotional tour exit and steps back from public life
items.description: The star makes an emotional farewell as she wraps up a tour she's described as her "last hurrah".

items.title: Remarkable US oil deal puzzles analysts - and angers many Venezuelans
items.description: Amounting to 65 billion barrels of crude, the deal is labelled by one ex-envoy as a colonialist "fever dream".

items.title: Could the man who murdered a Christian missionary and his sons walk free in India?
items.description: Dara Singh is serving a life sentence for burning alive Graham Staines and his two sons in Odisha in 1999.

items.title: Will self-flying planes transform the skies?
items.description: Autonomous crop-spraying aircraft are leading the way in pilot-free flying.

items.title: 'I've never been to Afghanistan': Six million deportees forced to start over under the Taliban
items.description: As of August, the number forced to return this year from Pakistan and Iran had reached another million.

items.title: Pistol in a lake gives hope for French cold case
items.description: Saad al-Hilli was shot dead with his wife and mother-in-law while holidaying in eastern France in September 2012.
